description: Defines a ScheduleDefinition + underlying asset job that materializes the configured asset keys on cron. Two modes: (1) un-partitioned — ScheduleDefinition with your cron; (2) time-partitioned — build_schedule_from_partitioned_job, cron is decomposed into minute_of_hour/hour_of_day/day_of_week/day_of_month args and combined with the partitions_def cadence (Dagster forbids passing a raw cron_schedule for time-partitioned jobs). Cron validated against partitions_def cadence; static/dynamic partitions rejected in the partitioned path with a helpful error.

schedule_name.label: Schedule Name
schedule_name.description: Unique schedule name shown in the UI.

cron_expression.label: Cron Expression
cron_expression.description: Cron expression (5 fields: m h dom mon dow). E.g. '0 9 * * *' = daily 09:00. REQUIRED when no partition fields are set; OPTIONAL when partitioned (cadence is inferred from the partitions_def; when supplied, cron is decomposed into offset args and validated against cadence).

asset_keys.label: Asset Keys
asset_keys.description: Slash-separated asset keys to materialize on each tick. Set this, asset_check_keys, or both.

job_name.label: Job Name
job_name.description: Name of the underlying job (defaults to '<schedule_name>_job').

execution_timezone.label: Execution Timezone
execution_timezone.description: IANA timezone for cron evaluation, e.g. 'America/Los_Angeles'. Applied in the un-partitioned path; in the partitioned path Dagster uses the partitions_def's timezone (this field is silently ignored).

tags.label: Tags
tags.description: Tags applied to runs created by this schedule.

partition_type.label: Partition Type
partition_type.description: Partition type: 'daily', 'weekly', 'monthly', 'hourly', 'static', 'multi', 'dynamic', or None for unpartitioned. Only time-based types work with the partitioned-job path.

partition_start.label: Partition Start
partition_start.description: Partition start in ISO format (e.g. '2024-01-01' or '2024-01-01-00:00' for hourly). Required for time-based types.

partition_values.label: Partition Values
partition_values.description: Comma-separated values for static or multi partitioning.

dynamic_partition_name.label: Dynamic Partition Name
dynamic_partition_name.description: Name for DynamicPartitionsDefinition (when partition_type='dynamic'). Rejected in the partitioned-schedule path.

partition_dimensions.label: Partition Dimensions
partition_dimensions.description: Multi-axis partition spec: list of {name, type, start, values, dynamic_partition_name} dicts. Overrides flat fields when set.

partition_cron_schedule.label: Partition Cron Schedule
partition_cron_schedule.description: Required when partition_type='cron'. A cron expression restricting the date axis to a custom cadence, e.g. '0 0 * * 1-5' for weekdays only (business-day cadence). Built on Dagster's TimeWindowPartitionsDefinition(cron_schedule=...).

partition_cron_fmt.label: Partition Cron Fmt
partition_cron_fmt.description: strftime format for partition keys produced by partition_type='cron'. Only change this for a sub-daily cron_schedule.

partition_end_offset.label: Partition End Offset
partition_end_offset.description: Passed through to the underlying Daily/Weekly/Monthly/Hourly/cron partitions definition. 0 (the Dagster default) means a time-based partition set only ever holds COMPLETED windows -- e.g. a daily set never includes today until tomorrow. Set to 1 to include the current, still-in-progress window.

partition_timezone.label: Partition Timezone
partition_timezone.description: IANA timezone for the underlying Daily/Weekly/Monthly/Hourly/cron partitions definition (defaults to UTC when unset, matching Dagster's own default).

asset_check_keys.label: Asset Check Keys
asset_check_keys.description: Asset check keys to run on each tick, as '<asset_key>:<check_name>' (asset key segments slash-separated, e.g. 'marts/orders:row_count_check'). Runs just the check -- via Dagster's real AssetSelection.checks(...), confirmed to execute with zero re-materialization of the parent asset -- for periodic re-validation without re-running the (possibly expensive) materialization. Combine with asset_keys to also materialize other assets in the same tick.

cadence.label: Cadence
cadence.description: 'scheduled' (default): normal cron/partitioned schedule, as below. 'once': mirrors Airflow's @once -- fires a single run the first time this component's sensor evaluates while RUNNING, then never fires again. Builds a sensor instead of a schedule, so it's mutually exclusive with cron_expression, partition_type/partition_dimensions, end_date, and add_logical_date_tag (none of those apply to a one-shot trigger).

end_date.label: End Date
end_date.description: ISO date or datetime (e.g. '2026-06-01'; a value with no timezone is assumed UTC) after which this schedule stops firing -- mirrors Airflow's DAG end_date. Un-partitioned: each tick is skipped once scheduled_execution_time reaches this date. Partitioned: ALSO passed to the partitions_def's own end_date (no partition past it is ever offered), in addition to the same tick-level skip. Only valid with cadence='scheduled'; requires cron_expression to be set explicitly even in the partitioned path (the auto-inferred-cadence cron used when end_date/add_logical_date_tag are both unset doesn't apply here).

add_logical_date_tag.label: Add Logical Date Tag
add_logical_date_tag.description: If true, tags each run with 'logical_date' -- Airflow's run-identifying timestamp. Partitioned: the partition window's start (Airflow's own definition: logical_date = start of the data interval). Un-partitioned: the scheduled trigger time. Only valid with cadence='scheduled'; requires cron_expression in the partitioned path (see end_date).

add_interval_tags.label: Add Interval Tags
add_interval_tags.description: If true, also tags each run with 'data_interval_start' / 'data_interval_end' (ISO8601) -- the window of data this run covers, for pipelines that process 'the interval that just ended' rather than a single point in time. Only meaningful for a partitioned schedule (the un-partitioned path has no interval concept -- a plain cron tick is a single trigger instant, not a window); requires partition_type/partition_dimensions to be set, and (like add_logical_date_tag) requires cron_expression explicitly in that path.

name: CronSchedule
